description: Jordan is holding their late grandfather's remaining woodworking tools and must decide which family member will receive each item, where the largest tool will be kept, and how the handoff will happen after checking in with Mina and Caleb.

shared_context.S1: The family is keeping three of their grandfather's workshop items: a benchtop planer, a scroll saw, and a locked chest of hand tools.
shared_context.S2: Jordan is storing the items temporarily and will make the final decisions about who receives each one.
shared_context.S3: The family wants the items to remain with relatives rather than being sold.
shared_context.S4: The planer is too large for ordinary car transport and needs a secure, level place to be kept.
shared_context.S5: Jordan's usual family check-in is to ask Mina and Caleb in turn about their plans, space, and practical details before settling the arrangement.
shared_context.S6: Only Jordan, Mina, and Caleb are participating in this decision; after both relatives have answered the check-in, Jordan makes the final call rather than waiting for input from anyone else.

PF1.text: Mina has promised to use the planer to build an accessibility ramp for their aunt, and her garage has a clear 120-centimeter west bench beside a 240-volt outlet; she has not yet told Jordan.

PF2.text: Caleb is restoring the unfinished birdhouse their grandfather started and specifically needs the grandfather's scroll saw for that project; he has a dry 90-centimeter shelf where it can remain set up, but he has not yet told Jordan.

acceptance_conditions: Mina must receive the benchtop planer.
The planer must be kept on Mina's 120-centimeter west garage bench beside the 240-volt outlet.
Caleb must receive the scroll saw.
Jordan must retain the locked chest of hand tools.
A commitment to transport and secure the planer at Mina's garage on the bench beside the outlet must exist.
A commitment to keep the scroll saw set up for Caleb's birdhouse restoration on his shelf must exist.
Caleb's birdhouse project must be cited as justification for the scroll saw assignment.

content_checks.C2: '120-centimeter' in decisions['planer_storage'] and 'west bench' in decisions['planer_storage'] and '240-volt' in decisions['planer_storage']
content_checks.C5: any('planer' in c['detail'] and 'Mina' in c['detail'] and '120-centimeter' in c['detail'] and '240-volt' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any('scroll saw' in c['detail'] and 'Caleb' in c['detail'] and 'birdhouse' in c['detail'] and 'shelf' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Mina's ramp promise and the exact 120-centimeter west bench beside a 240-volt outlet change the planer recipient to Mina, specify its storage location, and require a matching transport-and-secure commitment.
Caleb's unfinished birdhouse project and dry 90-centimeter shelf change the scroll saw recipient to Caleb and require a commitment to keep the saw set up on that shelf for the project.
